prompt: Hypothetical. Capital Rs 50,000, risk 1 percent. Entry Rs 252, stop Rs 247. The shares allowed are 49. What is the planned loss in rupees?
solution: Risk per share = 252 minus 247 = Rs 5. Planned loss = 49 multiplied by Rs 5 = Rs 245. Check: Rs 245 divided by 49 = Rs 5 per share.

prompt: Hypothetical. The same trade: 49 shares, entry Rs 252, stop Rs 247. The market opens at Rs 240. What is the actual loss in rupees if you leave at the open?
solution: Loss per share = 252 minus 240 = Rs 12. Actual loss = 49 multiplied by Rs 12 = Rs 588. Check: 50 multiplied by 12 = 600, and 600 minus 12 = 588.

prompt: Hypothetical. You planned a loss of Rs 245 on 49 shares. The market opens at Rs 240, below your stop. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The loss stays at Rs 245, because the stop was set.
The loss is 49 multiplied by Rs 12, which is Rs 588. That is more than the Rs 500 risk budget.
The loss equals the Rs 500 risk budget, because the stop limits it.
The stop at Rs 247 protects the loss at exactly that price.

explanations.a: A stop is a trigger, not a guarantee. A gap can open the price past the stop, so the loss can grow.
explanations.c: The loss is Rs 588 in this case. A stop does not cap the loss at the risk budget when a gap happens.
explanations.d: The market opened at Rs 240. The stop at Rs 247 did not hold the price. The exit came at the open.

prompt: Spot the mistake. A student writes: 'Set the stop at Rs 250, inside the zone of Rs 249 to Rs 252. No reason is needed for a stop inside a zone.' Which part is the mistake?

options.text: Inside the zone of Rs 249 to Rs 252.
No reason is needed for a stop inside a zone.

explanations.a: A stop price is a normal part of a plan. Rs 250 is not wrong by itself.
explanations.b: A zone is a band of prices. A stop can sit inside a zone when the plan gives a reason for it.
explanations.c: The mistake is the claim that no reason is needed. Every stop needs a stated reason that you can check.

prompt: Which prices give risk per share for a buy?

options.text: The entry price minus the stop price.
The entry price alone, because it is the price you paid.
The high of the zone minus the low of the zone.
The stop price plus the risk budget.

explanations.b: The entry price alone does not show how far the stop is from the entry. The stop sets the risk per share.
explanations.c: The zone range measures the band of prices. It does not show the loss from your stop.
explanations.d: The risk budget is a rupee amount you allow for the trade. It is not a price.

prompt: Which statement about passing the chart-reading assessment is correct?

options.text: Passing shows that you read the chart items correctly. It does not show that any chart method works.
Passing shows that chart methods work.
Passing proves that the zone levels will hold.
Passing means you can place live trades with confidence.

explanations.b: Reading items correctly is a skill. It is not evidence that any chart method earns money.
explanations.c: A zone is a band on a past chart. Nothing in the assessment shows that a level will hold in the future.
explanations.d: The assessment checks reading skills on sample items only. It does not test live trading, and it does not show that trading works.
